MythicCode.title: MythicCode
MythicCode.description: Represents a unique Mythic Code used for initial access and activation of club membership.

id.description: Unique identifier for the MythicCode entity.

code.description: The actual unique mythic code string provided to users for club access.

status.description: The current status of the mythic code, e.g., 'available' or 'activated'.

activationDateTime.description: Timestamp when the mythic code was activated.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile entity that activated this code. (Relationship: MythicCode 1:1 UserProfile)

UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Stores detailed information about a club member, associated with an activated Mythic Code.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

mythicCodeId.description: Reference to the MythicCode entity used by this user to gain initial access. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:1 MythicCode)

name.description: The full name of the club member.

email.description: The email address of the club member.

emergencyContact.description: Emergency contact phone number for the member.

registrationDateTime.description: Timestamp when the user profile was fully registered with additional details.

lastLoginDateTime.description: Timestamp of the user's last login.

rankingScore.description: The user's current score or rank within the club, for the ranking feature.

isPublicProfile.description: Indicates whether the user's profile is visible to other members.

profileImageUrl.description: An optional URL to the user's profile picture.

Pet.title: Pet
Pet.description: Records details about a pet owned by a club member, allowing for pet registration and linking to external monitoring services.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Pet entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile entity that owns this pet. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Pet)

dateOfBirth.description: The birth date of the pet.

weightKg.description: The weight of the pet in kilograms.

registrationDateTime.description: Timestamp when the pet was registered in the Hall Black Club app.

definition.description: Stores unique Mythic Codes. The `id` of the document is `mythicCodeId`. Includes denormalized `userId` once activated for authorization independence.

params.name: mythicCodeId
params.description: The unique identifier of the Mythic Code.

definition.description: Stores detailed user profiles. The `id` of the document is the user's Firebase Authentication UID, providing path-based ownership for authorization.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the user, matching their Firebase Authentication UID.

definition.description: Stores pets belonging to a specific user. The `userId` field within each pet document is denormalized from the parent UserProfile for authorization independence.

params.name: userId
params.description: The unique identifier of the pet's owner, matching their Firebase Authentication UID.

params.name: petId
params.description: The unique identifier of the pet.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for Hall Black Club is designed with security, scalability, and debuggability as top priorities, adhering to all mandated principles. 

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL) & Denormalization:**
1.  **UserProfile:** Each user's profile is stored at `/users/{userId}`, where `{userId}` is directly mapped to `request.auth.uid`. This path-based ownership inherently provides authorization independence, as the `uid` is part of the document's path, eliminating the need for `get()` calls to determine ownership for primary user data. The `UserProfile` entity has an `id` field which, in practice, will be the same as the Firebase `auth.uid`.
2.  **Pet:** Pets are stored as a subcollection under their owner: `/users/{userId}/pets/{petId}`. The `Pet` entity itself includes a `userId` field. This `userId` field is **denormalized** from the parent `UserProfile`. This means that security rules for a pet document can directly check `resource.data.userId == request.auth.uid` without needing to `get()` the parent `/users/{userId}` document. This ensures that creating, updating, or deleting a pet can be an atomic operation, independent of the parent `UserProfile`'s state for authorization purposes. This robust approach significantly simplifies security rules and prevents complex transactional issues.
3.  **MythicCode:** This collection holds codes that are activated by new users. The `MythicCode` entity includes a `userId` field which is populated upon activation. While the initial activation is handled by a backend serverless function (which inherently bypasses client-side rules), this `userId` field makes it easy to enforce read access for the associated user or for administrative purposes after activation, without needing to `get()` other documents.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
1.  **UserProfile:** `list` operations for a user's *own* profile are inherently secure due to path-based ownership (`/users/{request.auth.uid}`). For public profiles, `list` queries will need to filter on `isPublicProfile == true`. The structure allows rules to efficiently validate these queries, ensuring that a user can only query for profiles explicitly marked as public, thus preventing rules from acting as filters on sensitive data.
2.  **Pet:** `list` operations within `/users/{userId}/pets` are secure and efficient. A user can `list` their own pets by querying `/users/request.auth.uid/pets`. Because pets are directly nested under the user and contain the `userId` field, the rules can enforce that `request.auth.uid == userId` (from the path) and `request.auth.uid == resource.data.userId` (from the document) for any `list` operation, ensuring that only the owner can retrieve their pets. No unauthorized listing is possible because the path explicitly includes the owner's ID.
3.  **MythicCode:** The design assumes that users do not `list` `mythicCodes`. Instead, they `update` a *specific* code (via a serverless function) they already possess. This prevents information leakage about available codes, upholding the QAP by not allowing general `list` access for regular users. Admin `list` operations would be restricted to specific statuses (e.g., `available`).

**Structural Segregation & Access Modeling:**
*   **Private User Data:** `/users/{userId}` and `/users/{userId}/pets/{petId}` clearly segregate user-owned private data, making ownership explicit and rules straightforward.
*   **Global, Transactional Data:** `/mythicCodes/{mythicCodeId}` represents a collection with specific, controlled access patterns (mostly backend-driven updates), separate from user-specific data, to simplify its security posture.
